sentences: The detective gets a chance to watch a popular opera performance.
For seven years, the amnesiac opera star has been locked in an insane asylum, his identity a mystery – even to himself.
But when his memory unexpectedly returns, he begins to recall that his wife and her lover tried to murder him – and now he's determined to make them face the music.
The amnesiac escapes from the asylum and makes his way to the opera house and begins hiding out in the various rooms and passageways.
Soon, members of the opera company are being murdered one by one.
The detective soon investigates the killings and despite the presence of the amnesiac, there are other suspects who may be the real killer.

The suspects, excluding the amnesiac, include the diva, the opera company's prima donna who has been having a secret affair with the leading man, the baritone; the jealous husband, the diva's husband who has warned the leading man to stay away from his wife; the leading man's wife, the opera company's number two soprano who has learned of her husband's affair with the diva; and the young suitor, the fiancée of the diva's unacknowledged daughter who has been refused permission to marry the daughter.
Clues found by the detective to apprehend the killer include a torn newspaper, a charred note, a heel mark on a newspaper picture, and a bloodstained belt.

Among the questions asked are who has been threatening the diva's life, the mystery man in the leading man's dressing room before he is murdered, and why does the detective insist that the opera be performed twice in one evening?
The detective has been investigating the whereabouts of the heir, heir to a vast fortune.
He recently made contact with his relations in the city: his aunt, her daughters the first daughter and the second daughter, and the second daughter's husband, the son-in-law.
The story opens as the heir is traced to a ship that has sunk, but it cannot be confirmed that he is dead.
On the contrary, evidence is found that someone is trying to kill him to prevent his return to the city to claim the estate.
The heir arrives at the family house and is promptly murdered.
His body is revealed in the course of a seance conducted that evening at the family house with the detective in attendance.
He is an old friend of the aunt; who, like her late brother, is a devout believer in psychic research.
She has retained the services of the psychic researcher and his wife, the medium, who is a medium.
Someone subsequently attempts to kill the aunt and eventually appears to succeed.
The truth is revealed in another seance, at which the murderer makes a foolish mistake.
The inspector of the government department views a number of crashes and disappearances of the aviation company aircraft as suspicious.
With the test pilot, the inspector visits the company.
The test pilot test flies the aviation company aircraft but finds nothing wrong.
When a crash survivor claims that a mystery aircraft had attacked his plane, its owner, the businessman, hires the psychiatrist to question the man.
The psychiatrist believes that a psychotic ex-World War I flying ace, whom he dubs "the unknown pilot," may be responsible for the attacks.
With the help of the test pilot, the businessman and the psychiatrist assemble a group of five former flying aces who may have a connection with the mysterious unknown pilot.
He recruits the German lieutenant, the French lieutenant, the British captain, the Canadian lieutenant and the American lieutenant.
The group meets in a mansion to devise a plan for confronting the unknown pilot.
However, the German lieutenant comes under immediate suspicion because of his son, a former German prisoner of war.
On the team's first patrol, the unknown pilot attacks, killing the German lieutenant.
Later that day, the French lieutenant is killed by the unknown pilot and the next day, the British captain experiences a mental breakdown.
The test pilot receives a note from the unknown pilot asking him to meet him in the sky the next morning.
The Canadian lieutenant receives a similar note but the unknown pilot, who is on the airfield, paints an "X" on the Canadian lieutenant's aircraft.
The test pilot mistakes the Canadian lieutenant for the unknown pilot and kills him.
When a paint can is found in the American lieutenant's locker, all accuse him of being the unknown pilot.
That night, the psychiatrist calls the elder businessman, telling him that he knows the identify of the unknown pilot, but he is murdered.
The inspector believes that the test pilot is the unknown pilot and sends the American lieutenant and the British captain after him.
The young woman, the businessman's ward, however, first finds part of the British captain's goggles near the psychiatrist's dead body, then finds the other half in his aircraft.
The British captain pursues the test pilot with the young woman trapped on his aircraft.
Once in the sky, the unknown pilot appears and attacks the British captain, wounding him.
In a fierce dogfight, the unknown pilot attacks the test pilot but is downed.
In the wreckage of the unknown pilot's aircraft, the body of the businessman's son is discovered, along with a photograph of him in a German uniform.
He was not in fact a prisoner of war, but had deserted and joined the German air force.
With the mystery solved, the test pilot and the young woman realize that they are attracted to one another and embrace.

The film deals with a "problem the president submitted... whether it was possible for a man, weary of faithless friends and a wasted life, to convert a $5,000,000 estate into cash, disappear and start anew in some worth-while activity."

(cited from the newspaper – Monday, April 16, 2012) The disillusioned attorney is engaged by his friend the businessman to lobby on behalf of the large cannery company against a bill that would've empowered smaller businesses.
After the attorney is successful, he encounters the woman, who runs a cannery that is the main livelihood of the small town; the cannery has been forced to close because of the bill.
The attorney listens to the townsfolk and is inspired to help them.
The attorney liquidates his assets, closes his bank accounts, and stages a failed business venture to make it seem that he's gone bankrupt.
Once ready, he leaves his estranged wife to fake his death in a car accident.
The wife tries to inform the businessman, who is also her lover, about the attorney's strange behavior but is accidentally killed by the businessman's manservant.
The attorney learns about the wife's death through the radio, and how the attorney is blamed for it but the case is considered closed since his "body" was found by the police.
Some months later the attorney, using his new name, is in a relationship with the woman and has turned her cannery into a success.
They are visited by the businessman, who wants to buy out their business.
The businessman recognizes the attorney and tries to blackmail him into compliance.
When the attorney refuses, the businessman informs the police and the attorney is arrested for the wife's murder.
While the attorney is held in the town jail, the businessman plants agents provocateurs to cause a riot to destroy the cannery.

The attorney learns of this and, due to his good relationship with the people of the small town, is allowed out of the town jail to talk the rioters down and bring proof of his intentions to keep the cannery going.
Meanwhile, the attorney's former manservant, acting on his own initiative, finds out from the businessman's manservant that the wife's death was an accident.
The businessman is arrested for causing the riot, and the attorney is released, freeing him to marry the woman.
When the millionaire city businessman receives a death threat in the mail, he sends for his offspring.
The young man, a newspaper reporter turned lawyer, is dispatched by the newspaperman, his former editor, to track down the millionaire's daughter.
She does not appreciate being dragged away from the nightclub/casino of the club owner.
She and her perpetually drunk brother have also received similar mail.
When their other brother is killed in a car crash that night, the young man soon discovers it was not an accident; a wire cable strung across the road caused it.
The young man is pressured into investigating.
The millionaire's will leaves everything equally to his children.
If they predecease him, the estate goes to various charities.
The drunk brother is the next victim.
An associate of the club owner's is driving the drunk brother's car when he is stopped by the police.
They find the drunk brother's body inside with six shots to the head; the driver claims he did not know it was there when he stole the automobile.
The police captain of the homicide squad arrests the club owner, but has to release him for lack of evidence.
It turns out that the other brother is still alive and in hiding.
By the time the young man and the newspaperman track him down, though, he has been stabbed to death.
Next is the millionaire.
A man climbs down to his suite and, after a struggle, flings him over the terrace to his death.
To protect the daughter (to whom he has become attracted), the young man sets a trap.
He spreads the word that she is flying away at midnight, then gathers all the prime suspects at the club owner's nightclub to see her off.
Her drink is poisoned, but a doctor is standing by and she is saved.
The young man sadly identifies the killer; the newspaperman was the only one who had the opportunity to slip poison into the liquor.
The editor confesses that he needed more money to keep his wife happy.
He figured that with the millionaire's family all dead, he would be put in charge of one of their businesses.
Afterward, the young man and the daughter get married.
The detective is proud of his oldest son, the swimmer, being chosen to represent his country at the 1936 Summer Olympics in the foreign capital.
Meanwhile, over the skies of the detective's home city, the "company owner's plane" is demonstrating an improvement of remote radio control to the country's military.
The aircraft is hijacked by a concealed stowaway, the device stolen, and the test pilot murdered.
When the detective and his astute second son identify the stowaway, he finds only the man's body.
On the passenger list of the only aircraft to leave the home city for the mainland after the incident are the young pilot and the woman.
The young pilot was the intended test pilot, but injured his shoulder and had to be replaced.
He left on the airliner to travel to the Olympics himself as a competitor.
Perusing the list, the company owner recognizes the name of the arms dealer.
Several of the suspects head for the host country on with the national Olympic team.
The detective, the arms dealer, and the inventor arrive before them by taking the airship.
Aboard the ocean liner, the oldest son suspects the woman of being an "adventuress".
He spots her putting a piece of paper in her book, and the arms dealer taking it.
He confides in the fellow Olympian, the young pilot's girlfriend.
When the ship docks, the German inspector, the detective, and the company owner go to question the woman, only to find her gone and her cabin rifled.
The detective is reunited with his oldest son when the latter sneaks into the cabin through a porthole to play detective.
On the train trip to the foreign capital, the detective learns that the oldest son saw the woman borrow a camera from the girlfriend.
The arms dealer overhears the pair speculate that the invention was smuggled off the ship in it.
The arms dealer advises the detective to stop investigating, then spots a gun barrel in a passing car and pushes the pair to safety.
A shot strikes their compartment window.
Later, the arms dealer arranges for the girlfriend's camera to be stolen, but finds nothing inside.
A hotel maid tries to steal the invention, hidden in the girlfriend's candy box, but is foiled by the detective and the German inspector.
When she runs to the window to warn her accomplices, the detective substitutes a book for the device without being noticed.
The company owner insists on keeping the candy box in his hotel suite, where he is visited by the arms dealer.
The detective and a policeman break in when they hear gunfire.
They find the inventor on the floor.

He claims the arms dealer accused the company owner of taking the device to double-cross the stockholders of his company, then after the arms dealer left, the company owner took the invention at gunpoint and slugged him.
The woman takes the candy box to her employer, the diplomat.
When they discover the substitution, the woman surmises that the detective has the device.
The diplomat sends the detective a ticket to the Olympic opening ceremony.
While the detective verbally spars with him and the woman, the oldest son is kidnapped.
The detective allows himself to be taken to the diplomat to exchange the device for his son.
The company owner is brought in to verify it is the invention; he does (even though it is an imitation with a radio beacon inside).
Satisfied, the diplomat orders his men to dispose of the detective and his son when the arms dealer and his men burst in.
The arms dealer threatens to kill the oldest son if the detective does not produce the real equipment, but the police arrive just in time to rescue the detective.
The company owner is found unconscious from a gunshot in another room.
The inventor accuses the arms dealer of the shooting, but the detective proves that the inventor was responsible for that and also the murder of his accomplice back in the home city.
Afterward, the oldest son wins the 100 meter swim.

While the detective and his number one son are aboard a city-bound transatlantic liner returning from the foreign country in their previous adventure (the previous film), they have a run-in with a mysterious woman, who secretes a package in the trunk of the detective and his son.
After the liner docks, the detective and the son are met at the pier by the inspector and two rival reporters, the woman reporter and the man reporter.
The mysterious woman, who left the country hurriedly a year ago when sought as a material witness in a political scandal, has returned to "blow the lid off the town".
She follows the detective and his son to their hotel and attempts to regain her package from the trunk, only to be interrupted by the son.
She then goes to the "nightclub", where "candid-camera night" is in full swing, followed by the son.
Already present are the woman reporter and the man reporter.
The mysterious woman is mysteriously murdered and the detective is summoned from a police banquet in his honor.
Present in the room with the body are the club manager; the club dancer and the club manager's girl-friend and the two reporters.

While the detective seeks a motive for the murder, a second body is discovered in his hotel room, the package is missing from the detective's trunk, and it is realized that it must have contained her diary.
The detective neatly puts together a few scattered clues and then springs a trap to confirm the identity of the killer.
The son's efforts to aid in the investigation earn him two black eyes, one from the club manager and another from the murderer he tackles to save his father's life.
The professor (an actor) requests the detective's assistance in tracking down the sender of a few sinister letters, which killed two of the professor's acquaintances.
The prominent author (an actor), who is a cripple, is pinpointed by the detective as the culprit.

The detective rationally deduces that the author is out for payback — decades ago, a prank then-university scholar the professor and a group of chums played on the author went awry, causing him to be in his current state.
The professor shares with the detective that his daughter (an actress) is romantically involved with the author's elder brother (an actor).
With that, he quietly makes a move.
The detective arranges for all of the professor's surviving university pals to gather at his residence.
All agree to, except for the taxi driver (an actor).
The detective later learns that the two friends of the professor's were experiencing financial difficulties.
Meanwhile, the detective's partner (an actor) is sent to guard the author's house.
The author is also invited to join the meeting at the detective's house.
Just as he arrives, the doctor (an actor) is shot by a hidden assailant.
The detective, seeing the direction the shot came from, vouches for the author's innocence.
Some time later, both the partner and the detective are captured by the brother, who despises them for initially accusing the author of the wrongdoing.
They manage to break free and the inspector (an actor) promptly arrests the brother for kidnapping.
The detective suddenly cracks the case, after much thought into it.
He concludes that the author had indeed sent those letters, but they were just meant to frighten the recipients.
Instead, the actual murderer of the men is found to be one of the professor's friends, the banker (an actor).
The banker was the one who told the detective about the two men being in debt.
In actuality, the banker had stolen their money and made up the tale himself, as a spot-check on the men's backgrounds showed.
A Southern town is rocked by scandal when the teenage girl is brutally murdered on the campus of her business school on Confederate Memorial Day.
The crime quickly becomes a cause célèbre.
The prosecutor, a district attorney with political ambitions, sees the crime as his way to the Senate if he can find the right scapegoat to be tried for the girl's murder.
He seeks out the instructor, the girl's teacher.

Even though all evidence against the instructor is circumstantial, the instructor happens to be from the northern city, and the prosecutor works with the reporter to create a media frenzy of prejudice and hatred against the teacher.
The issue moves from innocence or guilt to the continuing bigotry and suspicion between South and North, especially given the significance of the day of the murder.
The trial attracts a famous Northern attorney, the defense lawyer, who agrees to defend the instructor.

Immense pressures begin to mount on members of the community to help in the conviction – the black janitor is induced to lie on the stand for fear he himself will be convicted if the instructor is found innocent; a juror serves as the sole holdout to a guilty verdict; and a local barber is afraid to testify to something he knows because it could exonerate the instructor.
The defense lawyer does his best, but the instructor is ultimately convicted of the girl's murder and sentenced to death.

The governor of the state, with the support of his wife, decides to commit political suicide by commuting the instructor's death sentence to life imprisonment because the evidence is simply insufficient to send a man to his death.

The townsfolk are enraged, and the girl's brothers, who have been threatening all along to take matters into their own hands if the instructor is not executed, plot and carry out the instructor's abduction and lynching with the help of a vengeful mob.
Afterward, the instructor's widow goes to the prosecutor's office to return a check he had sent her to help her out, telling him he cannot soothe his conscience that way.
As he and the reporter watch the widow leave the building, the reporter wonders if the instructor was guilty.
The prosecutor replies without much concern, "I wonder."
The film opens with the detective in disguise as a street salesmen and selling goods to passers-by.
He sees a man leaving a shop with a tattoo of the British flag on his arm.
The detective enters the shop to sell a rare diamond to the owner.
However, the detective sees a body stuffed into a wicker basket in the store, and using his mastery of judo takes down the shopkeeper.
Later, he reserves a stateroom on a passenger ship headed for the port city.
Also on the liner is the young man, son of the owner of the shipping line.
Before leaving, the father gives his son a confidential letter for the head of the port city branch of the company.
The young man and the detective become friends (the detective notices the letter), and the detective helps the young man cure a hangover.
The young man complains to the detective that he has not met any beautiful women on board.
After a stop in the island port, a beautiful woman using an assumed name (not her real name) boards the ship, and she and the young man fall in love.
But the beautiful woman is a spy for the smuggling boss, who runs a smuggling operation out of the port city.
She periodically sends him notes and leaves without saying goodbye to the young man.
The detective finds a steward looking for the young man's letter and confronts him, knowing he was the person who killed the man in the wicker basket, as he wears the tattoo.
The detective throws the man overboard and takes the letter.
At the port city, the young man meets with the branch manager.
The branch manager and gives him the letter, but later learns that it is a blank sheet of paper.
He calls his father, who tells him the letter said to watch out for smugglers.
The young man is determined to find the beautiful woman, and he learns from an unknown person that she is at the nightclub.
Both he and the branch manager go there, as well as the detective and his date.
The young man finds the beautiful woman performing at the club and goes to her dressing room.
However, the club owner, the smuggling boss, discovers them together and, knowing that the young man knows too much, locks them both up.
The detective tells the date to call the police, and seeks out the smuggling boss.
Posing as a fellow smuggler, he tricks the smuggling boss into leading him to the beautiful woman and the young man.
The date is shot while contacting the police, but manages to tell them where she is.
The branch manager finds the smuggling boss, and demands that the beautiful woman and the young man be released.
The smuggling boss finds out that the detective is not a smuggler, then the detective apprehends him.
The detective tells the branch manager to get the smuggling boss's gun, the gun explodes as the branch manager tries to grab it, killing the smuggling boss.
Police storm the building, and the detective tells them the branch manager headed the smuggling operation.
The branch manager replaced the letter and shot the date.
The detective gave the branch manager the opportunity to kill the smuggling boss, who knew he was in on the plot, and he did.
The branch manager is arrested, and things go back to normal.
